title: Malabsorption Labs: Fecal Elastase-1 and Coeliac Serology with Total IgA
summary: Learn how fecal elastase-1 points to pancreatic insufficiency and why its cut-off is soft, what fakes a low result, and why IgA anti-TG2 coeliac serology always needs a total IgA level, with IgG tests and biopsy in IgA deficiency.

reviewer.note: Teaches Ch. 23 Hit 13 (fecal elastase-1, 200 μg/g, weak for mild disease, unaffected by enzyme replacement), Hit 14 (anti-tTG IgA first line; total IgA; IgG serology in IgA deficiency) and Trap 6 (negative tTG-IgA in IgA deficiency). Checked against the European PEI guideline (Dominguez-Muñoz 2025), the UK PEI practical guidelines (Phillips 2021), the FE-1 meta-analysis (de la Iglesia 2025) and the ESsCD 2025 adult coeliac guideline Part 1 (Al-Toma 2025). The 200 μg/g cut-off is taught as frequently used but not firmly established (register flag rv-fe1-soft-cutoff); the reviewer’s ~2% IgA deficiency is given as 2–3% and the guideline’s biopsy rule is added (register flag rv-celiac-igad-biopsy). Not taught: the reviewer’s “use human/recombinant tTG” antigen advice (not found in the sources read) and the 5–6× concentration figure from Memory Hooks.

objectives: Interpret fecal elastase-1 results at 200 and 100 μg/g, including the effect of pretest probability.
Identify pre-analytical problems that falsely lower fecal elastase-1 and recognise that enzyme replacement does not interfere.
Explain why total IgA must accompany IgA anti-TG2 serology and what to do in IgA deficiency.

scenes.title: Two negatives that are not negative
scenes.altText: Invented scenario: an adult with months of greasy, loose stools and weight loss. Three result cards: (1) fecal elastase-1 160 μg/g, lab comment “watery sample”; (2) IgA anti-tissue transglutaminase (anti-TG2) negative; (3) total serum IgA below 7 mg/dL. Question token: “Pancreas, gut lining, or neither?”

cues.text: Invented case: an adult with months of greasy, loose stools and weight loss. Is the pancreas failing, or the lining of the small bowel?
Fecal elastase comes back low, on a watery sample. The coeliac antibody, IgA anti-transglutaminase, is negative. And total IgA is almost undetectable.
So is it the pancreas, the gut lining, or neither? Two of these results may not mean what they seem.

props.label: Invented case: greasy loose stools · weight loss

scenes.title: Two tests, two organs
scenes.altText: Two cards. Left, fecal elastase-1 (FE-1): an enzyme made only by the pancreas that is not broken down in the gut, is concentrated as it passes, and reflects total pancreatic secretion; a small stool sample is enough and it is stable at room temperature for 3 days. Right, coeliac serology: IgA anti-TG2 by ELISA is the preferred first-line test; IgA anti-endomysial antibody (EMA) is highly specific but labour-intensive and operator-dependent. Bottom token: both rely on the right sample — formed stool for FE-1, a gluten-containing diet for serology.

cues.text: Two tests, two organs. Fecal elastase-1 is an enzyme made only by the pancreas. It is not broken down in the gut, it is concentrated on the way through, and it reflects total pancreatic secretion.
A small amount of stool is enough, and the enzyme is stable at room temperature for about three days.

For the bowel lining, the preferred first-line coeliac test is IgA antibody to tissue transglutaminase, by ELISA. The endomysial antibody is highly specific, but labour-intensive and operator-dependent.
Serology only works while the patient is still eating gluten: on a gluten-free diet, the antibodies typically normalise.

scenes.title: How low is low? Fecal elastase cut-offs
scenes.altText: Scale bar for FE-1: below 200 μg/g suggests moderate pancreatic exocrine insufficiency (PEI), below 100 μg/g severe PEI (UK practical guidelines). Sensitivity card: at <200 μg/g, sensitivity 25–65% in mild, 82–100% in severe PEI (UK). Meta-analysis card (13 studies, 888 patients, mostly chronic pancreatitis and cystic fibrosis): pooled sensitivity 0.94, specificity 0.69 at 200 μg/g; at 100 μg/g, specificity 0.82, sensitivity 0.88. Guideline token (European 2025): no single cut-off can be established, though 200 μg/g is frequently used; false positives in low pretest probability, false negatives in high.

cues.text: The lower the fecal elastase, the more likely the pancreas is failing. Below two hundred micrograms per gram suggests moderate insufficiency; below one hundred suggests severe.
It catches severe disease well, but misses much mild disease: in UK guideline data, sensitivity at two hundred was as low as twenty-five to sixty-five percent in mild insufficiency.

A 2025 meta-analysis, mostly of chronic pancreatitis and cystic fibrosis studies, found sensitivity of ninety-four percent but specificity of only sixty-nine percent at two hundred. Dropping the cut-off to one hundred raised specificity and lowered sensitivity.

European guidelines say no single cut-off can be established, although two hundred is widely used. In low-risk patients, a low result may be a false positive; in high-risk patients, a normal result may be a false negative.

scenes.title: Sample problems that fake results
scenes.altText: Left column, stool: watery stool dilutes the specimen and gives falsely low FE-1; measure on a formed sample, or adjust to a standard water content and repeat (UK; European guideline prefers formed stool). Pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy (PERT) does not affect FE-1 because the assay detects human elastase only. Right column, serum: measure total IgA alongside IgA-based serology; IgA deficiency affects 2–3% of people with coeliac disease and is more common than in the general population; total IgA deficiency is serum IgA below 7 mg/dL. In total IgA deficiency use IgG-based tests (IgG anti-TG2 or IgG anti-DGP); a negative IgG test does not exclude coeliac disease, and with malabsorption, duodenal biopsy is indicated regardless. Hook answers card.

cues.text: Watery stool dilutes the sample and pushes fecal elastase falsely low. Test a formed stool when possible, or ask the lab to correct for water content and repeat.
Enzyme capsules do not interfere: the assay detects human elastase only, so pancreatic enzyme replacement can continue.

For coeliac serology, measure total IgA at the same time. IgA deficiency affects two to three percent of coeliac patients. Below seven milligrams per decilitre, use IgG tests: IgG anti-transglutaminase or IgG anti-deamidated gliadin peptide.

Back to the hook. The elastase should be repeated on a formed or water-adjusted sample. The negative IgA test cannot be trusted in IgA deficiency; with malabsorption, duodenal biopsy is needed even if IgG tests are negative.

props.label: Hook: repeat FE-1 on formed stool · IgG tests + biopsy

scenes.title: Three classic traps
scenes.altText: Three trap cards: “A negative IgA anti-TG2 rules out coeliac disease” (✓ not without a total IgA level, and not on a gluten-free diet); “Stop enzyme capsules before fecal elastase” (✓ the assay detects human elastase only; PERT does not affect it); “FE-1 below 200 on watery stool proves pancreatic insufficiency” (✓ dilution lowers FE-1; repeat on formed stool and weigh the pretest probability).

cues.text: Trap one: a negative IgA transglutaminase test rules out coeliac disease. Not without a total IgA level, and not if the patient has stopped eating gluten.
Trap two: stop enzyme capsules before testing fecal elastase. No: the assay measures human elastase only, so replacement therapy does not affect it.
Trap three: an elastase below two hundred on watery stool proves pancreatic insufficiency. No: dilution lowers it. Repeat on formed stool, and weigh the pretest probability.

props.title: ✗ “Negative tTG-IgA rules out coeliac.”
lines: ✓ Check total IgA; patient must eat gluten

scenes.title: Postcards and messengers
scenes.altText: Memory aid: “Elastase is a POSTCARD the pancreas mails through the gut: it arrives intact, so count postcards per gram of stool. Pour water on the pile and the count per gram falls. IgA is the MESSENGER that carries the coeliac message: no messenger (IgA deficiency), no message, so ask the IgG messenger and look at the bowel itself.” Tokens: postcard = elastase · water = dilution · messenger = IgA. A card lists where the aid breaks.

cues.text: Memory aid: elastase is a postcard the pancreas mails through the gut. It arrives intact, so you count postcards per gram of stool, and pouring water on the pile lowers the count. IgA is the messenger for the coeliac message: no messenger, no message, so ask the IgG messenger and look at the bowel itself.

Where it breaks: there is no sharp cut-off for elastase, and its accuracy depends on pretest probability; mild insufficiency is often missed; and IgG tests are less sensitive, so a negative one does not exclude coeliac disease.

props.title: Where it breaks
lines: No sharp FE-1 cut-off; depends on pretest risk
Negative IgG test does not exclude coeliac

scenes.title: Takeaway
scenes.altText: Two tokens: “FE-1: < 200 moderate · < 100 severe · watery stool = false low · enzymes don’t interfere”, “Coeliac: IgA anti-TG2 + total IgA · IgA < 7 mg/dL → IgG tests ± biopsy”.

cues.text: Read a low fecal elastase-1 against stool consistency and pretest probability, and never accept a negative IgA anti-transglutaminase result without a total IgA level, because watery stool and IgA deficiency both produce false answers.

props.label: FE-1: < 200 moderate · < 100 severe · watery = false low
Coeliac: IgA anti-TG2 + total IgA · IgA < 7 → IgG ± biopsy

explanation.what: Plain language: when someone cannot absorb food, the fault is often either a pancreas that makes too few digestive enzymes or a damaged bowel lining, as in coeliac disease. A stool enzyme test checks the pancreas; a blood antibody test checks for coeliac disease, but only if the body can make that antibody class. Scientific terms: fecal elastase-1 (FE-1), pancreatic exocrine insufficiency (PEI), pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy (PERT), pretest probability, IgA anti-tissue transglutaminase (anti-TG2, tTG-IgA), anti-endomysial antibody (EMA), anti-deamidated gliadin peptide (DGP), selective and total IgA deficiency, duodenal biopsy.
explanation.why: FE-1 is pancreas-specific and survives intestinal transit, so its stool concentration tracks pancreatic secretion; dilution by watery stool lowers the concentration per gram. IgA anti-TG2 is an IgA antibody, so a patient who cannot make IgA cannot produce a positive result.
explanation.measure: FE-1 <200 μg/g suggests moderate and <100 μg/g severe PEI; sensitivity at <200 is 25–65% in mild and 82–100% in severe PEI; pooled sensitivity 0.94 and specificity 0.69 at 200 μg/g (0.88/0.82 at 100 μg/g). Formed stool preferred; watery samples water-adjusted and repeated; stable ~3 days at room temperature; PERT does not interfere. Coeliac: IgA anti-TG2 ELISA first line on a gluten-containing diet with total IgA; total IgA deficiency <7 mg/dL → IgG anti-TG2 or IgG anti-DGP; negative IgG does not exclude; biopsy if malabsorption.
explanation.differs: FE-1 (pancreatic secretion) vs coeliac serology (mucosal autoimmunity); IgA-sufficient (IgA anti-TG2 valid) vs total IgA deficiency (IgG-based tests, biopsy); high vs low pretest probability for interpreting FE-1.
explanation.examAngle: Expect: the next step after a negative tTG-IgA with low total IgA, whether to stop enzymes before FE-1, why a watery stool gives a low FE-1, and which FE-1 level suggests severe insufficiency.

questions.stem: An adult with chronic diarrhoea, weight loss and iron deficiency has a negative IgA anti-TG2 while eating gluten. Total serum IgA is below 7 mg/dL. What is the best next step?

options.text: IgG-based serology (IgG anti-TG2 or IgG anti-DGP), with duodenal biopsy given the malabsorption
options.rationale: Correct. In total IgA deficiency, IgA tests cannot be positive; IgG tests are used, and with malabsorption a biopsy is indicated whatever the IgG result.
Incorrect. IgA deficiency causes false-negative IgA-based serology.

options.text: Repeat IgA anti-TG2 after a gluten-free diet
options.rationale: Incorrect. Antibodies typically normalise on a gluten-free diet, and IgA tests still cannot work in IgA deficiency.

options.text: Repeat the IgA anti-TG2 by a different ELISA kit
options.rationale: Incorrect. Changing kits does not overcome the absence of IgA.

questions.stem: A patient taking pancreatic enzyme capsules is referred for fecal elastase-1. What should the laboratory advise?

options.text: Continue the capsules; the assay detects human elastase only
options.rationale: Correct. FE-1 assays measure human elastase, so replacement therapy does not affect the result.

options.text: Stop the capsules for 5 days before collection
options.rationale: Incorrect. Stopping is unnecessary because the enzyme in the capsules is not measured.
Incorrect. FE-1 needs only a small stool sample; timed collections are for faecal fat.

options.text: Collect a watery sample after a laxative for better recovery
options.rationale: Incorrect. Watery stool dilutes the sample and gives falsely low results; formed stool is preferred.

questions.stem: Which fecal elastase-1 statement is best supported?

options.text: Below 100 μg/g suggests severe pancreatic exocrine insufficiency
options.rationale: Correct. UK practical guidelines read <200 μg/g as moderate and <100 μg/g as severe insufficiency.

options.text: Above 200 μg/g reliably excludes mild insufficiency
options.rationale: Incorrect. Sensitivity at 200 μg/g is only about 25–65% in mild insufficiency.

options.text: A low value in a low-risk patient confirms insufficiency
options.rationale: Incorrect. Specificity is only moderate, so in low-risk patients a low result may be a false positive.

options.text: A watery sample gives falsely high values
options.rationale: Incorrect. Dilution gives falsely low values.

accuracyFlags.issue: Ch. 23 Hit 13 presents 200 μg/g as the FE-1 cut-off. The 2025 European PEI guideline states that a cut-off cannot be established although 200 μg/g is frequently used, that low pretest probability produces false positives, and that formed stool should be used; UK guidelines add that watery samples give falsely low results (register flag rv-fe1-soft-cutoff).

Ch. 23 Hit 14 and Trap 6 give ~2% IgA deficiency and advise IgG serology (DGP-IgG). ESsCD 2025 gives 2–3%, allows IgG anti-TG2 or IgG anti-DGP, and adds that a negative IgG result does not exclude coeliac disease, so patients with malabsorption need duodenal biopsy regardless (register flag rv-celiac-igad-biopsy).
